required_outcomes: Reads the tenant's "Thank you!" as an acknowledgement of the agency's email, with no question or new fact in it.
Keeps the job waiting for the landlord, who was asked on 13 September, with a dated review or follow-up at or after the 3-day landlord window (around 16-17 September).
Records why no further action is needed now (for example a short note that the landlord was asked less than a day ago and the tenant has only acknowledged).
acceptable_alternatives: A short reply to the tenant saying the landlord has been asked and when she will next hear, provided it invents no date for a visit.
Asking the tenant whether there is a wall switch for the hood near the hob that might be off, as a quick self-check while the landlord decides.
positive_behaviours: Uses the existing landlord wait rather than opening a second approval request.
red_flags: Chasing the landlord, or re-sending the approval request, a few hours after he was first asked.
Escalating to a human because a message arrived.
prohibited_actions: Assigning a contractor or returning the ticket to provider selection without the landlord's answer.
Closing or cancelling the request on the strength of the tenant's "Thank you!".
critical_failures: Closing the job or dispatching a contractor without landlord approval on the basis of the tenant's thanks.
